BURSEVI:v10p367/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p367/r1.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p367/r1.claim: The Prophet said that if Abu Jahl summoned his council, the torment angels would have been called into view.
BURSEVI:v10p367/r1.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "لو دعا ناديه الزبانية عيانا".

BURSEVI:v10p367/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p367/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p367/r7.claim: Kalla is a renewed rebuke connected with what precedes; the pause after it is therefore treated as an absolute pause.
BURSEVI:v10p367/r7.anchor: {كلا} ردع بعد ردع للناهي المذكور وزجر له أثر زجر فهو متصل بما قبله ولذا جعلوا الوقف عليه وقفا مطلقا

BURSEVI:v10p367/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p367/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p367/r8.claim: Do not obey the lying, sinful forbidding man; persist in prostration and prayer without concern for him, and draw near to God through prostration.
BURSEVI:v10p367/r8.anchor: كقوله تعالى : {لا تطعه واسجد} وواظب على سجودك وصلاتك غير مكترث به {واقترب} وتقرب بذلك السجود إلى ربك

BURSEVI:v10p367/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p367/r9.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p367/r9.claim: A hadith says the servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating, so believers should pray abundantly then.
BURSEVI:v10p367/r9.anchor: وفي الحديث : "أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه إذا سجد فأكثروا من الدعاء في السجود"

BURSEVI:v10p367/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p367/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p367/r10.claim: In the hadith’s grammar, mā is a verbal noun, aqrab is a subject with an omitted predicate, and yakūn is complete; it means the servant’s closest presence with God occurs in prostration.
BURSEVI:v10p367/r10.anchor: كلمة ما مصدرية وأقرب مبتدأ حذف خبره ويكن تامة أي أقرب وجود العبد من ربه حاصل وقت سجوده.

QASHANI:96:15/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:96:15/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:96:15/r2.claim: Do not obey the opponent; remain in monotheism. Prostration is annihilation in attentive prayer, drawing near through annihilation of acts, attributes, and essence until abiding in God without residual selfhood.
QASHANI:96:15/r2.anchor: لا توافقه ودم على ما أنت عليه من مخالفته بملازمة التوحيد

QASHANI:96:15/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:96:15/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QASHANI:96:15/r3.claim: In this prostration the Prophet seeks refuge through God’s act from His act, attribute from attribute, and essence from essence, embodying the three stages of approach.
QASHANI:96:15/r3.anchor:
ولهذا قرأ عليه السلام في هذه السجدة:
" أعوذ بعفوك من عقابك "

QASHANI:96:15/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:96:15/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QASHANI:96:15/r4.claim: A hadith says the servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating.
QASHANI:96:15/r4.anchor:
وفي الحديث:
" أقرب ما يكون العبد إلى ربه إذا سجد "

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r18.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r18.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r18.claim: The servant approaches the witnessing of Lordship with his heart while remaining on the ground of servanthood with his self; alternatively, prostrate bodily and draw near through the secret.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r18.anchor: اقترب من شهود الربوبية بقلبك ، وقف على بساط العبودية بنفسك . ويقال : فاسجد بنفسك ، واقترب

SULAMI:v2p407#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p407#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p407#3/r1.claim: Approach the court of Lordship, having been released from the court of servanthood.
SULAMI:v2p407#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ^ ( اقترب ) ^ إلى بساط الربوبية فقد اعتقناك

SULAMI:v2p407#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p407#3/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p407#3/r2.claim: Common people remain within servanthood's attributes; the elect are honored by divine qualities and witness no other attributes, while commoners cannot bear them because their inner secrets are weak and distant from truth's source.
SULAMI:v2p407#3/r2.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمه الله : العوام متقلبون في صفات العبودية ، والخواص

SULAMI:v2p407#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p407#3/r3.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p407#3/r3.claim: The limbs must manifest worship's beauty, expressing Lordship over servanthood; the body returns to dust, and one can approach only by being drawn near, as 56:88 indicates.
SULAMI:v2p407#3/r3.anchor: وقال الحسين : في هذه الآية معناه أن الله لم يبح للجوارح ترك التجلي بمحاسنها

SULAMI:v2p407#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p407#3/r4.speaker: ذو النون
SULAMI:v2p407#3/r4.claim: Permission to prostrate shows that God has drawn one near; the servant should approach inwardly, in keeping with the report that the nearest state is prostration.
SULAMI:v2p407#3/r4.anchor: وقال ذو النون : في قوله : ﴿ واسجد واقترب ﴾ قال : إذا رأيت اني أذنت

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3451#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3451#3/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3451#3/r1.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reads the command to prostrate as addressed to Muhammad and the invitation to draw near as addressed to Abu Jahl, in a threat.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3451#3/r1.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم قال : واسجد انت يا محمد واقترب انت يا أبا جهل يتوعده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r1.claim: The revelation paused after the first five verses; during the pause Muhammad continued to see Gabriel and receive non-Qur’anic revelation, while the duration is not important.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r1.anchor: الوحي فتر بعد نزول الآيات الخمس الأوائل من هذه السورة وتلك الفترة الأولى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r2.speaker: السهيلي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r2.claim: Al-Suhayli says the revelation pause lasted two years; Ibn Ashur considers that duration unlikely.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r3.speaker: الحربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r3.claim: Al-Harbi says before the Night Journey the Prophet prayed once before sunset, meaning Asr, and once before sunrise, meaning Fajr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r3.anchor: ذكر الحربي أن الصلاة قبل الإسراء كانت صلاة قبل غروب الشمس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r4.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r4.claim: Yahya ibn Salam gives the same account and says the Night Journey and prescription of the five prayers occurred a year before the Hijra.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r5.claim: The early prayer was a distinct, still-unregulated form of worship involving prostration, performed publicly; Abu Jahl objected and forbade it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r5.anchor: بل كانت هيئة غير مضبوطة بكيفية وفيها سجود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r6.claim: The rest of the surah followed the opening verses after a short interval, when the Prophet had begun praying and news of revelation had spread; consecutive recitation normally reflects consecutive revelation, and al-Alaq was the first surah revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r6.anchor: الأصل في الآيات المتعاقبة في القراءة أن تكون قد تعاقبت في النزول إلا ما ثبت تأخره بدليل بين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r7.claim: The statement that the human transgresses when he considers himself self-sufficient introduces the account of the man who forbids prayer and its continuation through the command not to obey him.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r5.claim: The closing passage sums up the previous argument: the Prophet should keep praying in the Sacred Mosque and not fear Abu Jahl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r5.anchor: هذا فذلكة للكلام المتقدم من قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r6.claim: “Do not obey him” uses obedience metaphorically for fear or caution, meaning that Abu Jahl cannot harm the Prophet; the command to prostrate underscores prayer, and “draw near” praises its nearness to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r6.anchor: وأطلقت الطاعة على الحذر الباعث على الطاعة على طريق المجاز المرسل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r7.claim: The form “iqtarib” conveys effort and seeking: strive to draw near to God through prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r7.anchor: عبر بصيغة الافتعال لما فيها من معنى التكلف والتطلب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r7.claim: Kalla refutes the unbeliever; Muhammad must not heed his prohibition or words, but should prostrate and draw near through worship and good deeds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r7.anchor: ثم قال تعالى لمحمد عليه السلام: كلا ردا على قول هذا الكافر وأفعاله لا تطعه أي لا تلتفت إلى نهية وكلامه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r8.claim: A prophetic report says the servant is closest to his Lord while prostrating, so he should pray often then, when prayers are likely to be answered.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r8.anchor: وفي الحديث أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه إذا سجد، فأكثروا من الدعاء في السجود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r9.claim: Mujahid adds: then He said, “Did you not hear: prostrate and draw near?”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ثم قال ألم تسمعوا: واسجد واقترب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r10.speaker: ابن وهب عن جماعة من أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r10.claim: They say “prostrate” addresses Muhammad and “draw near” addresses Abu Jahl, challenging him to approach and see his destruction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r10.anchor: وروى ابن وهب عن جماعة من أهل العلم أن قوله تعالى: واسجد خطاب لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وأن اقترب خطاب لأبي جهل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r11.speaker: جماعة من أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r11.claim: A group of scholars says this surah contains a prostration, including Ibn Wahb in the Maliki school.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r11.anchor: وهذه السورة فيها سجدة عند جماعة من أهل العلم، منهم في مذهب مالك ابن وهب.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r1.claim: Kalla rejects Abu Jahl's position; Muhammad must not obey him by leaving prayer, but should prostrate and draw near to God through obedience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r1.anchor: كلا أي ليس الأمر على ما عليه أبو جهل لا تطعه في ترك الصلاة واسجد أي صل لله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r2.claim: The majority take the command to draw near as addressed to the Prophet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r2.anchor: وهذا قول الجمهور أن قوله تعالى واقترب خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r3.claim: One alternative addresses both men: Muhammad is told to prostrate, while Abu Jahl is told to approach the Fire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r3.anchor: أحدهما أن المعنى اسجد انت يا محمد واقترب أنت يا أبا جهل من النار قاله زيد بن أسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r4.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r4.claim: A report from some early authorities treats the command to draw near as a threat to Abu Jahl, supported by the earlier report about his encounter with the Prophet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r4.anchor: والثاني واقترب يا أبا جهل تهددا له رواه أبو سليمان الدمشقي عن بعض القدماء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r5.claim: The Prophet says a servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating, so worshippers should make abundant supplication then.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#4/r5.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439#2/r1.claim: Muhammad must not obey the one who forbids worship; he may pray wherever he wishes because God protects and supports him, and he should prostrate and draw near.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {كلا لا تطعه} يعني: يا محمد، لا تطعه فيما ينهاك عنه من المداومة على العبادة وكثرتها، وصل حيث شئت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says a servant is closest to his Lord while prostrating, so worshippers should increase supplication; Muslim transmits it as sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد، فأكثروا الدعاء"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439#2/r3.claim: The Prophet also prostrated during recitation of Surat al-Inshiqaq and Surat Iqra.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439#2/r3.anchor: وتقدم أيضا: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يسجد في: {إذا السماء انشقت} و {اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق}

JISHUMI:v10p7482/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r4.claim: “Prostrate and draw near” commands the Prophet to pray and approach God through sustained obedience; Abū Jahl cannot harm him, for God protects him.
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r4.anchor: قيل: تقرب إلى الله بالمواظبة على طاعته فإن أبا جهل وغيره لا يقدرون على مضرتك، فالله يعصمك،

JISHUMI:v10p7482/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r5.claim: Another reading commands Muḥammad to prostrate and threatens Abū Jahl that approaching will bring punishment; the author says the surah is addressed to the Prophet.
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r5.anchor: وقيل: اسجد أنت يا محمد، واقترب يا أبا جهل، فالأول أمر، والثاني تهديد،

JISHUMI:v10p7482/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r8.claim: No creature is to be obeyed in disobeying the Creator.
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r8.anchor: على أنه لا طاعة لمخلوق في معصية الخالق

KASHSHAF:96:19/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:19/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:19/r1.claim: Kalla rebukes Abu Jahl; do not obey him but persist in what you are doing, as in the cited verse.
KASHSHAF:96:19/r1.anchor: { كَلاَّ } ردع لأبي جهل { لاَ تُطِعْهُ } أي اثبت على ما أنت عليه من عصيانه

KASHSHAF:96:19/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:19/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:19/r2.claim: Prostration means continuing to pray, and drawing near means approaching one's Lord.
KASHSHAF:96:19/r2.anchor: { واسجد } ودم على سجودك ،   يريد : الصلاة

KASHSHAF:96:19/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:19/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF:96:19/r3.claim: A hadith says the servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating.
KASHSHAF:96:19/r3.anchor: أقرب ما يكون العبد إلى ربه إذا سجد

KASHSHAF:96:19/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF:96:19/r4.claim: A report promises the reward of reciting the whole Mufassal section to the one who recites Surat al-ʿAlaq.
KASHSHAF:96:19/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصّل كله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r13.claim: Kalla rebukes Abu Jahl; do not obey him, persist in prostration and prayer, and draw near your Lord.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r13.anchor: { لا تطعه } أي اثبت على ما أنت عليه من عصيانه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r14.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r14.claim: The Prophet says a servant is nearest to his Lord when prostrating.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r14.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( 1326 ) ( أقرب ما يكون العبد إلى ربه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r1.claim: Kalla la tuti'hu means do not obey Abu Jahl.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r1.anchor: قال أبو هريرة : كلا لا تطع أبا جهل في أمره .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r2.claim: One gloss is not to accept Abu Jahl's command or opinion if he draws near.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r2.anchor: أحدهما : لا تقبل قوله إن دارك ولا رأيه إن قاربك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r3.claim: Another gloss is not to answer his words or retaliate for his action.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r3.anchor: الثاني : لا تجبه عن قوله , ولا تقابله على فعله , ومنه ما روي عن النبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r4.claim: The Prophet prayed, Allah, do not answer a traveler among us: a traveler may ask for rain to stop, whose answered prayer would ruin people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r4.anchor: ومنه ما روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( اللهم لا تطع فينا مسافرا ) أي لا تجب دعاءه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r5.claim: One interpretation tells Muhammad to prostrate and Abu Jahl to approach the Fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r5.anchor: أحدهما : اسجد أنت يا محمد مصليا , واقترب أنت يا أبا جهل من النار , قاله زيد بن أسلم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r6.claim: The alternative tells Muhammad to prostrate in prayer and draw near his Lord, since a servant is closest to God in prostration.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r6.anchor: الثاني : اسجد أنت يا محمد في صلاتك لتقرب من ربك , فإن أقرب ما يكون العبد إلى الله تعالى

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r7.claim: A report says 84 verses were revealed about Abu Jahl, 104 about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and 32 about al-Nadr ibn al-Harith.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r7.anchor: وروى جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال : أنزل في أبي جهل أربع وثمانون آية , وأنزل في الوليد بن المغيرة مائة وأربع آيات

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r8.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r8.claim: A report transmitted through Ata al-Khurasani gives an ordered revelation list: 85 Meccan surahs, then 27 Medinan, and omits al-Fatiha as far as the author knows; the author calls it the fullest account despite many disagreements.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r8.anchor: فكان أول ما نزل فيما بلغنا : ( اقرأ باسم ربك ) ثم ( ن والقلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r9.claim: Most scholars say al-Alaq was the first surah revealed; among differing chronology reports, the author finds the transmitted list fullest and most satisfying.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p309/r9.anchor: وإذا كانت هذه أول سورة نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قول الأكثرين فقد روي في ترتيب السور بمكة والمدينة أحاديث

MUQATIL:96:9-19/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r7.claim: The Prophet must not obey the prohibition on prayer, but must prostrate and draw near. Polytheists began with prostration, then bowed, stood, and asked idols; God later changed the Prophet's order to standing, bowing, then prostrating.
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r7.anchor: لأنهم كانوا يبدؤون بالسجود، ثم بعد السجود بالركوع

MUQATIL:96:17-19/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:17-19/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:17-19/r2.claim: The Prophet is told not to obey Abū Jahl by abandoning prayer; prostration means prayer to God and drawing near means obeying Him.
MUQATIL:96:17-19/r2.anchor: يقول للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: لا تطع أبا جهل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#12/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#12/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#12/r1.claim: The rebuke is directed at Abu Jahl; the Prophet must persist in disobeying him, continue the prayer and prostration, and draw near to God, for the servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#12/r1.anchor: ﴿ كلا ﴾ ردع لأبى جهل ﴿ لا تطعه ﴾ أى اثبت على ما أنت عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r1.claim: Kalla denies Abu Jahl's expectation; Muhammad must not obey him by abandoning prayer, but should pray to God and approach through obedience and worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r1.anchor: أي ليس الأمر على ما يظنه أبو جهل. { لا تطعه } أي فيما دعاك إليه من ترك الصلاة.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r2.claim: Another interpretation says that while prostrating, the worshipper should approach God through supplication.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r2.anchor: وقيل: المعنى: إذا سجدت فاقترب من الله بالدعاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r3.claim: Ata reports Abu Hurayra transmitting the Prophet's saying that the servant is closest and most beloved to God when his forehead is on the ground in prostration.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r3.anchor: روى عطاء عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r4.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r4.claim: The scholars explain prostration as the culmination of servitude and humility before God's unmatched might; greater distance from the human condition brings nearness to Paradise and God's abode.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r4.anchor: قال علماؤنا: وإنما كان ذلك لأنها نهاية العبودية والذلة ولله غاية العزة،

QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r5.claim: A sound hadith instructs worshippers to glorify God in bowing and strive in supplication during prostration, when prayers are likely to be answered.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r6.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r6.claim: The cited couplet says that when necks humble themselves before God, their dignity lies in that very abasement.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r6.anchor: ولقد أحسن من قال: وإذا تذللت الرقاب تواضعا

QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r7.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r7.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam interprets the command as Muhammad prostrating in prayer while Abu Jahl approaches the Fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r7.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: اسجد أنت يا محمد مصليا، واقترب أنت يا أبا جهل من النار.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r8.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r8.claim: Prostration could mean prayer prostration or the recitation prostration; Ibn al-Arabi says prayer is the apparent sense from the context, but the sound report from Abu Hurayra in Muslim explicitly establishes a recitation prostration here.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r8.anchor: قال ابن العربي: «والظاهر أنه سجود الصلاة» لقوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r9.claim: Abu Hurayra says he prostrated with the Prophet in al-Inshiqaq and in Iqra, establishing that this passage involves prostration of recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r9.anchor: لولا ما ثبت في الصحيح من رواية مسلم وغيره من الأئمة عن أبي هريرة أنه قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r10.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r10.claim: A report from Ali says the four obligatory prostration passages are Alif Lam Mim, Ha Mim Tanzil, al-Najm, and Iqra; Ibn al-Arabi notes that accepting this implies a second prostration in al-Hajj, though it occurs with bowing.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r10.anchor: وقد روى ابن وهب، عن حماد بن زيد، عن عاصم بن بهدلة، عن زر بن حبيش، عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r11.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r11.claim: Ibn Nafi and Mutarrif say Malik privately prostrated at the end of this sura, while Ibn Wahb considered it one of the obligatory prostrations.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19/r11.anchor: وقد قال ابن نافع ومطرف: وكان مالك يسجد في خاصة نفسه بخاتمة هذه السورة

QURTUBI-FULL:96:19#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19#2/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19#2/r1.claim: A report transmitted through Malik, Rabi'a, and Nafi says that when this sura was revealed the Prophet told Muadh to write it; the tablet, pen, and inkwell bowed and prayed for exalted remembrance, removal of burdens, and forgiveness, after which Muadh and the Prophet prostrated.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:19#2/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لمعاذ: «اكتبها يا معاذ» فأخذ معاذ اللوح والقلم والنون

QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r1.claim: The believer must not obey the tyrant who forbids prayer and the call; he should prostrate, draw near to God through worship, and leave the tyrant to the Zabaniya.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r1.anchor: لا تطع هذا الطاغي الذي ينهى عن الصلاة والدعوة .  واسجد لربك

QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r5.claim: The warning applies generally to every obedient believer who worships and calls to God, and every arrogant aggressor who forbids prayer and threatens obedience.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r5.anchor: وكل طاغ باغ ينهى عن الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r1.claim: Kalla rebukes Abu Jahl: his boastful assembly cannot help him, he is too weak to resist the Prophet, and he will not make the Prophet obey his ban on prayer; it may also mean ‘no, do not obey him.’

RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r2.claim: Do not obey Abu Jahl, as in the parallel prohibition against obeying deniers.

RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r3.speaker: أكثر أهل التأويل
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r3.claim: Most exegetes interpret ‘prostrate’ as pray and devote oneself to God's worship through action and preaching, without fretting over the enemy because God will support the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r3.anchor: وعند أكثر أهل التأويل أراد به صل وتوفر على عبادة الله تعالى فعلا وإبلاغا

RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r4.claim: Some interpret ‘prostrate’ more generally as submission or humility.

RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r5.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r5.claim: Others understand the command as the physical prostration in prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل المراد نفس السجود في الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r6.claim: Approaching means seeking nearness to God through prostration; a prophetic report says a servant is closest to his Lord while prostrating.
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه إذا سجد )

RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r7.claim: Another interpretation addresses Abu Jahl: Muhammad should prostrate and Abu Jahl approach to see the zabaniya seize him, with the prayer increasing the unbeliever's rage as believers' devotion enrages them.
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r7.anchor: اسجد يا محمد ، واقترب يا أبا جهل منه

RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r8.claim: On a further sarcastic reading, Abu Jahl is told to put his foot on the praying Prophet, who is occupied with himself; the taunt belittles Abu Jahl.
RAZI-FULL:v32p26/r8.anchor: ثم قال عند ذلك : { واقترب } منه يا أبا جهل وضع قدمك عليه

STUDYQURAN:96:6/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:96:6/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:96:6/r11.claim: “Nay” can rebuke Abū Jahl or address the Prophet and followers to ignore his threats and continue prostrating.
STUDYQURAN:96:6/r11.anchor: Nay is either another rebuke to Abū Jahl or an address directly to the Prophet and his followers

STUDYQURAN:96:6/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:96:6/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:96:6/r12.claim: More generally, believers should ignore denials of religion or prayer and draw near to God through prostration; a hadith says prostration is a servant's closest state to the Lord.
STUDYQURAN:96:6/r12.anchor: The closest that a servant can be to his Lord is when he is prostrating

STUDYQURAN:96:6/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:96:6/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:96:6/r13.claim: This is one of fifteen verses after whose recitation prostration is enjoined.
STUDYQURAN:96:6/r13.anchor: This verse is one of fifteen verses after the recitation of which one is enjoined to prostrate

TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl’s threat, his sudden retreat from a trench of fire, awe and wings, and the Prophet’s statement that angels would tear him apart; the passage gives the revealed sequence.
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: قال أبو جهل: هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم؟ قال: فقيل: نعم، قال: فقال: واللات والعزى لئن رأيته

TAB-FULL:v24p541#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p541#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p541#2/r1.claim: Qatada says the verse was revealed over Abu Jahl’s threat to trample Muhammad’s neck; the Prophet said the angels would snatch him away if he tried.
TAB-FULL:v24p541#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {كلا لا تطعه واسجد واقترب} [العلق: 19] ذكر لنا أنها نزلت في أبي جهل، قال: لئن رأيت محمدا يصلي لأطأن عنقه

TABATABAI:96:11-19/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r12.claim: The renewed rebuke adds emphasis; ‘do not obey him’ means do not obey his ban on prayer, as the following command to prostrate shows that sajda here is prayer.
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r12.anchor: تكرار الردع للتأكيد، وقوله { لا تطعه } أي لا تطعه في النهي عن الصلاة

TABATABAI:96:11-19/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r13.claim: The Prophet’s prayer at that time may have consisted of glorifying God and prostrating to Him.
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r13.anchor: ولعل الصلاة التي كان صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يأتي بها يومئذ كانت تسبيحه تعالى

TABATABAI:96:11-19/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r14.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r14.claim: Another view takes the command as prostration upon reciting this surah, one of the Qur’an’s four obligatory prostrations.
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r14.anchor: وقيل المراد به السجود لقراءة هذه السورة التي هي إحدى العزائم الأربع

TABATABAI:96:11-19/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r15.claim: Iqtirāb means drawing near to God.

TABATABAI:96:11-19/r16.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r16.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r16.claim: A further interpretation takes ‘draw near’ to mean approaching God’s reward.
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r16.anchor: وقيل الاقتراب من ثواب الله تعالى

TABATABAI:96:1-19#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-19#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABATABAI:96:1-19#2/r1.claim: The cited Prophet report says a servant is closest to God while prostrating.
TABATABAI:96:1-19#2/r1.anchor: وفي المجمع في الحديث عن عبد الله بن مسعود أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

TABATABAI:96:19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:19/r1.speaker: الرضا
TABATABAI:96:19/r1.claim: Imam al-Rida likewise says the servant is nearest to God when prostrating, and connects this to ‘prostrate and draw near.’
TABATABAI:96:19/r1.anchor: سمعت الرضا عليه السلام يقول أقرب ما يكون العبد من الله وهو ساجد

TABATABAI:96:19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:19/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن سنان عن أبي عبد الله
TABATABAI:96:19/r2.claim: Imam al-Sadiq names four obligatory prostrations of recitation—al-Sajda, Ha Mim Sajda, al-Najm, and al-ʿAlaq—and says other Qur’anic prostrations are recommended.
TABATABAI:96:19/r2.anchor: وفي المجمع روى عبد الله بن سنان عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال العزائم الم التنزيل

ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r8.claim: Kallā denies Abū Jahl's claim; the Prophet should not obey him but should prostrate and draw near to God through obedience.
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r8.anchor:
أي ليس الأمر على ما عليه أبوجهل.
(لا تطعه واسجد واقترب)
أي وتقرب إلى ربك بالطاعة.

TABRISI:96:16-19/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:16-19/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:16-19/r8.claim: Kalla rejects Abu Jahl's position: do not obey his ban on prayer; prostrate to God and draw near to His reward.
TABRISI:96:16-19/r8.anchor: ليس الأمر على ما عليه أبو جهل

TABRISI:96:16-19/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:16-19/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:96:16-19/r9.claim: Drawing near means approaching God through obedience; the servant is closest to God while prostrating, or the command means pray to God.
TABRISI:96:16-19/r9.anchor: اسجد يا محمد للتقرب منه فإن أقرب ما يكون

TABRISI:96:16-19/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:16-19/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود عن النبي
TABRISI:96:16-19/r10.claim: The Prophet said that a servant is closest to God while prostrating.
TABRISI:96:16-19/r10.anchor: أقرب ما يكون العبد من الله إذا كان ساجدا

TABRISI:96:16-19/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:16-19/r11.speaker: عبد الله بن سنان عن أبي عبد الله
TABRISI:96:16-19/r11.claim: Prostration at the end of this surah is obligatory; the four obligatory recitation prostrations are in al-Sajda, Fussilat, al-Najm, and this surah, while all others are recommended.
TABRISI:96:16-19/r11.anchor: وما عداها في جميع القرآن مسنون وليس بمفروض

THALABI:v10p246/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p246/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p246/r8.claim: Do not obey Abū Jahl; instead prostrate, pray, and draw near to God.
THALABI:v10p246/r8.anchor: كلا لا تطعه واسجد واقترب وصل واقترب من الله سبحانه وتعالى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p182/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p182/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p182/r1.claim: Kallā rejects Abū Jahl's position; do not obey him by abandoning prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p182/r1.anchor: ثم قال: {كلا} (¬5) أي ليس الأمر على ما عليه أبو جهل. {لا تطعه} في ترك الصلاة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p182/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p182/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p182/r2.claim: Prostrate by praying to God and draw near to Him through obedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p182/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: وصل لله واقترب إليه بالطاعة (¬6).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p182/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p182/r3.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p182/r3.claim: Draw near to God; a servant is nearest to Him while prostrating. Mujāhid gives a similar gloss.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p182/r3.anchor: وقال عطاء: اقترب إلي، فإن العبد أقرب ما يكون من الله إذا هو سجد (¬7).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p182/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p182/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p182/r4.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أي تقرب إلى ربك بطاعته (¬1)

WAHIDI-QT:96:19/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:19/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:19/r1.claim: The situation is not as Abu Jahl thinks: do not obey him; pray and draw near to God through obedience.
WAHIDI-QT:96:19/r1.anchor: { كلا } ليس الأمر على ما عليه أبو جهل { لا تطعه واسجد } وصل { واقترب } تقرب إلى ربك بطاعته

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:18-19/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:18-19/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:18-19/r3.claim: Abu Jahl's expectation is false; the Prophet must not obey him, but pray and draw near to God through obedience.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:18-19/r3.anchor: كلا } ليس الأمر على ما عليه أبو جهل { لا تطعه واسجد } وصل { واقترب } تقرب

ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r7.claim: The repeated warning means not to heed the arrogant liar who forbids prayer, but to obey the Lord, continue reciting, and prostrate.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r7.anchor: Ona itaat etme öyle müstağnî yalancı, cânî, namazdan nehyeder azgını dinleme

ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r8.claim: A sound hadith says the servant is closest to the Lord while prostrating; a qudsi hadith says continued voluntary worship draws the servant near until God guides his hearing, sight, and heart.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r8.anchor: kulun rabbine en yakın olabileceği hâl secde ederkendir

ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r9.claim: Prostration may mean prayer in light of the earlier reference, but its literal sense is more apparent because “draw near” already covers prayer and other worship; separately naming prostration stresses its importance as perfect humility and submission.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r9.anchor: Burada “secde” yukarıdaki salât karînesiyle namaz mânasına olmak dahi muhtemil ise de hakikati üzere bilhassa kendi mânasında olmak daha zâhirdir

ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r10.claim: The two Sahih collections establish that the Prophet performed recitation prostration in both Surat al-Inshiqaq and this sura; the author urges readers to prostrate and keep drawing near to God.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r10.anchor: Sahîheyn’de sâbit olduğu üzere Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm اِذَا السَّمَٓاءُ انْشَقَّتْ’da ve bu sûrede tilâvet secdesi yapmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r4.claim: The repeated kallā indicates the tyrant will not dare summon supporters; Muhammad must not obey him but continue prayer and prostration, through which a servant draws nearest to God, as the Prophet taught.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r4.anchor: namaz kılmaya ve secde etmeye devam ederek Allah’a yakınlaşma gayretlerini sürdürmesi emredilmiştir

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:19:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:19:anmerkung/r1.speaker: Neuwirth; Uri Rubin
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:19:anmerkung/r1.claim: The call to prostrate may reflect part of the pre-Islamic prayer ritual, following Neuwirth's use of Uri Rubin.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:19:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Der erste Imperativ ruft zur Niederwerfung auf, die Neuwirth im Rekurs auf Uri Rubin für einen Teil bereits des vorislamischen Gebetsrituals hält

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:19:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:19:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:19:anmerkung/r2.claim: The second imperative is less concrete and probably calls generally for participation in worship; other sura endings also call for worship and praise, while some call for proclamation.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:19:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Der zweite Imperativ ist weniger konkret und wohl allgemein auf die Teilnahme an gottesdienstlichen Übungen zu beziehen

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:19:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:19:anmerkung/r3.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:19:anmerkung/r3.claim: The closing call functionally resembles the psalmic hallelujah, for example Psalm 149:9.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:19:anmerkung/r3.anchor: der psalmische Schlussruf הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ (“Lobet den Herrn”) zu vergleichen

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r2.claim: Kallā introduces verse 15, as it does the rebuke in verses 6–8 and the final call in verse 19.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r2.anchor: Die im Diesseits angesiedelte Szene der vorangehenden Verse schlägt hier offenbar in eine Vorausblende des Jüngsten Tages um

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r5.claim: The closing imperatives shift from speaking about the accused to addressing the Messenger and summarize the surah.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r5.anchor: Die Rede über den Angeschuldigten springt hier in eine Anrede an den Verkünder über, die in gewisser Hinsicht noch einmal die ganze Sure zusammenfasst

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r6.claim: The surah contrasts the evil one's worldly authority, which forbids prayer, with God's absolute authority and demand for obedience and worship.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r6.anchor: Der innerweltlichen Autorität des Bösen, der die Gebetsteilnahme untersagt, setzt sich die die absolute Autorität des göttlichen Sprechers entgegen

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r7.claim: The final command to worship returns to the opening command to recite in verses 1 and 3 (Neuwirth).
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r7.anchor: Die abschließende Aufforderung zum Gottesdienst führt dabei zugleich zu der am Surenanfang stehenden Anweisung zur Rezitation (iqraʾ, V. 1 und 3) zurück

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p383/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p383/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p383/r2.claim: The Prophet should persevere, forbear, disregard the rebels' provocations, prostrate, and draw near to God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r4.claim: The Prophet is assured to ignore anyone who blocks his prostration and draw nearer to God through it; prayer brings perseverance and divine help, and prostration is its greatest component.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r4.anchor: he should just ignore him and draw nearer the Almighty by prostrating before Him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r5.claim: Prostration is the objective of the Prophet’s life and his sole means of relationship with God, so he should seek refuge in God through it if challenged.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r5.anchor: The only way to do this is to prostrate before Him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r6.claim: To determine a sūrah’s revelation period, tone, addressee, and style are especially useful; the author therefore considers this question after the explanation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r6.anchor: The most helpful thing in determining the period of revelation of a sūrah is to deliberate on its tone, address and style of address

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r4.claim: The author considers al-‘Alaq a coherent, single unit: its first five verses share the rest’s severe tone, and nothing in it indicates revelation in two episodes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r4.anchor: The tone of its first five verses is no different

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p385/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p385/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p385/r1.claim: Mujāhid says a servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating and glosses the command as ‘prostrate and draw near.’
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p385/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r1.claim: Kalla rebukes Abu Jahl; do not obey him means pay no heed to his prohibition or speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r1.anchor: كلا: ردع لأبي جهل، ورد عليه في: لا تطعه: أي لا تلتفت إلى نهيه وكلامه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r2.claim: The command to prostrate means to persist in prayer; prostration names the act in which the servant is nearest to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r2.anchor: واسجد: أمر له بالسجود، والمعنى: دم على صلاتك، وعبر عن الصلاة بأفضل الأوصاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r3.claim: Approach means draw near to your Lord.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r4.claim: Both Ṣaḥīḥ collections record the Prophet prostrating during Sūrat al-Inshiqāq and this sūra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r4.anchor: وثبت في الصحيحين سجود رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r5.claim: ʿAlī counts this sūra among the obligatory prostration passages; Mālik used to prostrate in it in private.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r5.anchor: وهي من العزائم عند علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes Abu Jahl again; do not obey him means persist in worship, prostration, and drawing near to God despite him. Prostration may be literal or a metonym for prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r1.anchor: كلا ردع لذلك اللعين بعد ردع وزجر له أثر زجر لا تطعه أي دم على ما أنت عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits a Prophetic report in Muslim and others: the servant is nearest his Lord while prostrating, so one should make abundant supplication.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r2.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم وغيره من حديث أبي هريرة مرفوعا أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد فأكثروا الدعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r3.speaker: ثوبان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r3.claim: Thawbān transmits a sound Prophetic report urging frequent prostration: each prostration raises a degree and removes a sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r3.anchor: وفي الصحيح وغيره أيضا من حديث ثوبان مرفوعا عليك بكثرة السجود فإنه لا تسجد لله تعالى سجدة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r4.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r4.claim: On these and similar reports, more than one scholar holds that prostration is the best pillar of prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r4.anchor: ولهذه الأخبار ونحوها ذهب غير واحد إلى أن السجود أفضل أركان الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r5.speaker: العز بن عبد السلام
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r5.claim: Al-ʿIzz ibn ʿAbd al-Salām unusually held that supplication while prostrating is obligatory.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r5.anchor: ومن الغريب أن العز بن عبد السلام من أجلة أئمة الشافعية قال بوجوب الدعاء فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r6.claim: Authentic reports say the Prophet prostrated at the recitation of al-Inshiqāq and this sura; ʿAlī counted this sura among the prostrations of recitation, and Mālik prostrated here in private.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188#2/r6.anchor: وفي البحر ثبت في الصحيحين أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام سجد في إذا السماء انشقت وفي هذه السورة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r6.claim: Kalla rejects Abu Jahl's position; the Prophet must not obey him by abandoning prayer, but should pray and draw near to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r6.anchor: كلا} ليس الأمر على ما عليه أبو جهل، {لا تطعه} في ترك الصلاة، {واسجد} صل لله {واقترب} من الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r7.claim: The Prophet says a servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating and should make abundant supplication then.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r2.claim: كلا rebukes the forbidding person again; the Prophet must persist in obedience, continue prostrating, and draw near to God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r2.anchor: ردع أيضا للناهي. { لا تطعه } أي أثبت أنت على طاعتك

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r3.claim: A Prophetic report says a servant is nearest his Lord while prostrating.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r3.anchor: أقرب ما يكون العبد إلى ربه إذا سجد

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.claim: A report promises the reciter a reward as though he had recited the entire set of shorter suras.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

BINTSHATI:v2p33/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r6.speaker: المفسرون
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r6.claim: Exegetes take the pronoun in do not obey him as referring to Abu Jahl, while the apparent context and the preceding pronouns point to the person who disbelieved and turned away.
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r6.anchor: وظاهر السياق عود الضمير على الذي {كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى}

BINTSHATI:v2p34/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p34/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p34/r1.claim: Sujud means submission; the Quran applies it to the angels’ bow before Adam and to Yusuf’s family falling in prostration before him.
BINTSHATI:v2p34/r1.anchor: والسجود في العربية الخضوع، ومنه في القرآن الكريم: سجود الملائكة لآدم بأمر الله

BINTSHATI:v2p34/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p34/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p34/r2.claim: Worshipful prostration is ancient: Abraham and Ishmael were told to purify the sanctuary for worshipers, and pre-Islamic Arabs also bowed to their idols.
BINTSHATI:v2p34/r2.anchor: وفيما يتلو علينا القرآن من نبأ إبراهيم والبيت العتيق

BINTSHATI:v2p34/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p34/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p34/r3.claim: Islam abolished prostration to anything but the Creator and made sujud in prayer the climax of humble worship; mosques take their name from this act, and the Kaaba is al-Masjid al-Haram.
BINTSHATI:v2p34/r3.anchor: حتى نسخ الإسلام بنوره ظلام الوثنية وأبطل السجود لغير الخالق، وأخذ السجود دلالته الإصطلاحية على السجدة في الصلاة

BINTSHATI:v2p34/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p34/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p34/r4.claim: The command may refer specifically to prayer-prostration, as some exegetes say, while retaining the broader sense of complete humility shown by Quranic descriptions of the faithful.
BINTSHATI:v2p34/r4.anchor: وتخصيص السجود بالذكر في آية العلق، يقبل تأويله بالسجود في الصلاة كما ذهب بعض المفسرين

BINTSHATI:v2p35/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p35/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p35/r1.claim: Other passages describe believers prostrating at night, upon hearing revelation, and in worship; the Prophet is also commanded to praise God and prostrate.
BINTSHATI:v2p35/r1.anchor: وأمر الرسول بالسجود في آية العلق، نظيره ما في آيات

BINTSHATI:v2p35/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p35/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p35/r2.claim: She rejects Abu Hayyan’s interpretation of اقترب as seek closeness through devotion and prefers its direct sense of nearness: the worshiper is nearest to God while prostrating.
BINTSHATI:v2p35/r2.anchor: ولا نطمئن إلى تفسير الأقتراب هنا بالتقرب كما ذهب "أبو حيان"

BINTSHATI:v2p35/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p35/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p35/r3.claim: Ending with nearness names the worshiper’s highest aspiration; the Prophet’s prostration breaks the proud man’s vanity and answers the human illusion of independence, since God owns both afterlife and first life.
BINTSHATI:v2p35/r3.anchor: وإذ يأخذ الأقتراب من الله مكانه ختاماً للآية، وليس بعد القربى من الخالق غاية يطمح إليها العابد الساجد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r7.claim: The Prophet must not obey the man who forbids worship; he should continue praying and humbling himself, with prostration representing both prayer and worship generally.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r7.anchor: أي دم على صلاتك وخضوعك بنفسك وجدد ذلك في كل وقت

BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r8.claim: Prostration brings the servant nearest to God, so he should strive inwardly for nearness and affection through every act of worship, especially prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r8.anchor: فإنه أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r9.speaker: الغزالي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r9.claim: Al-Ghazālī reads the prayer of refuge as a spiritual ascent: first witnessing God's acts, then His attributes, then His essence, ending in loss of awareness of the self and recognition that God alone praises Himself.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r9.anchor: كما قال الإمام الغزالي في كتاب الشكر - مشاهدة أفعاله الله فقط

BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r10.claim: The Prophet moved through spiritual stations, treating earlier ranks as deficient by comparison; his repeated seeking forgiveness seventy times a day reflects this ascent.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r10.anchor: إنه ليغان على قلبي حتى أستغفر الله في اليوم والليلة سبعين مرة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r11.speaker: عائشة
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r11.claim: ʿĀʾisha asked why the Prophet wept and exerted himself in prostration although his past and future sins were forgiven.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r11.anchor: ولما قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها : قد غفر الله لك ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r12.claim: The Prophet answered that he should be a grateful servant, which the author interprets as seeking further spiritual stations because gratitude brings increase.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r12.anchor: معناه : أفلا أكون طالبا للمزيد في المقامات

BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r13.claim: The author says gratitude is the reason for increase, citing God's promise to increase those who give thanks.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r13.anchor: فإن الشكر سبب الزيادة حيث قال تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p489/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p489/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p489/r1.claim: The author cites Abraham's scroll advising the wise person to guard the tongue, understand the times, and attend to his own affairs.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p489/r1.anchor: ينبغي للعاقل أن يكون حافظا للسانه عارفا بزمانه مقبلا على شأنه

DURR-FULL:v8p565/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r8.claim: He takes ‘prostrate and draw near’ as telling Muhammad to prostrate while threatening Abu Jahl.
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r8.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم قال {واسجد} أنت يا محمد {واقترب} أنت يا أبا جهل يتوعده

DURR-FULL:v8p565/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r9.claim: He says a servant is nearest to his Lord in prostration, citing the command to prostrate and draw near.
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r4.claim: Prostration brings nearness to God (96:19); repeated prayer raises the worshipper’s rank until even minor sins become repugnant to him, let alone major ones.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r4.anchor: فإذا زادت قربته وارتفعت منزلته حتى صار أميرا

RAZI-FULL:v1p85/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p85/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p85/r1.claim: Shaytan derives from distance, whereas the obedient servant is near; the nearness of God and the command to draw near support this contrast.

TAB:96:17/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB:96:17/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Abu Jahl threatened to trample the praying Prophet, then recoiled, describing a fiery trench, terror, and wings; the Prophet said angels would tear him limb by limb, while attribution of the quoted revelation is uncertain.
TAB:96:17/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ،   قال :  قال أبو جهل :  هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم

TAB:96:19/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:19/r1.speaker: author
TAB:96:19/r1.claim: God rejects Abu Jahl's command: Muhammad must not stop praying, but prostrate and draw near to God through loving obedience; Abu Jahl cannot harm him because God protects him.
TAB:96:19/r1.anchor: لا تطع أبا جهل فيما أمرك به من ترك الصلاة لربك

TAB:96:19/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:19/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:96:19/r2.claim: Qatada says the verse was reported to have been revealed after Abu Jahl threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying.
TAB:96:19/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {  كلا لا تطعه واسجد واقترب } ذُكر لنا أنها نزلت في أبي جهل

TAB:96:19/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:19/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:96:19/r3.claim: The Prophet said that if Abu Jahl carried out his threat, the zabāniya would snatch him away.
TAB:96:19/r3.anchor: قال نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين بلغه الذي قال أبو جهل ،   قال :  «لو فعل لاختطفته الزبانية »

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p235#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p235#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p235#2/r3.claim: The root of sujūd is lowering or leaning: a camel lowers itself to be mounted, and a palm tree prostrates when it bends.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p235#2/r3.anchor: وأصل السجود: التطأطؤ والميل، يقال: سجد البعير وأسجد: إذا طؤطىء ليركب، وسجدت النخلة: إذا مالت

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p235#2/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p235#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p235#2/r5.claim: A person placing his forehead on the ground is called sā jid because he bends down; sujūd also means submission, obedience, and humility.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p235#2/r5.anchor: ومن هذا قيل لمن وضع جبهته بالأرض: ساجد، لأنه تطامن في ذلك. ثم قد يستعار السجود فيوضع موضع الاستسلام والطاعة والذل

ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r1.claim: Kallā is a rebuke restraining Abū Jahl.
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r1.anchor: { كلا } : ردع لأبي جهل ،   ورد عليه في : { لا تطعه }

ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r2.claim: The command means not to heed Abū Jahl’s prohibition or speech.

ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r3.claim: The command to prostrate means to continue praying; prayer is named through its finest posture, when the servant is nearest to God.
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r3.anchor: { واسجد } : أمر له بالسجود ،   والمعنى : دم على صلاتك ،   وعبّر عن الصلاة بأفضل الأوصاف

ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r4.claim: Iqtarib means draw near to your Lord.
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r4.anchor: العبد فيها أقرب إلى الله تعالى ،   { واقترب } : وتقرّب إلى ربك

ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r5.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r5.claim: The Prophet’s prostration at this sūra and at Idhā al-samāʾ inshaqqat is established in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections.
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r5.anchor: وثبت في الصحيحين سجود رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في { إذا السماء انشقت } وفي هذه السورة

ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r6.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib counted this among the obligatory prostrations of recitation.
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r6.anchor: وهي من العزائم عند علي بن أبي طالب

ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r7.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r7.claim: Mālik used to prostrate at this verse in his private practice.
ABUHAYYAN:96:19/r7.anchor: وكان مالك يسجد فيها في خاصية نفسه

ALUSI:96:19/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:19/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:19/r1.claim: Kallā again restrains and rebukes the tyrant after the earlier rebuke.
ALUSI:96:19/r1.anchor: ردع لذلك اللعين بعد ردع وزجر له أثر زجر

ALUSI:96:19/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:19/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:19/r2.claim: Do not obey him: persist in opposing him and in your worship.
ALUSI:96:19/r2.anchor: أي دم على ما أنت عليه من معاصاته

ALUSI:96:19/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:19/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:19/r3.claim: Continue prostrating without being intimidated; sajdah may mean literal prostration or stand metaphorically for prayer.
ALUSI:96:19/r3.anchor: وواظب غير مكترث به على سجودك وهو على ظاهره أو مجاز عن الصلاة

ALUSI:96:19/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:19/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:19/r4.claim: Draw near to your Lord by prostrating.

ALUSI:96:19/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:19/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI:96:19/r5.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet said that a servant is nearest his Lord while prostrating, so worshippers should make abundant supplication.
ALUSI:96:19/r5.anchor: وغيره من حديث أبي هريرة مرفوعاً أقرب ما يكون العبد

ALUSI:96:19/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:19/r6.speaker: ثوبان
ALUSI:96:19/r6.claim: Thawbān reports the Prophet urged frequent prostration: each prostration raises the servant one rank and removes one sin.
ALUSI:96:19/r6.anchor: من حديث ثوبان مرفوعاً عليك بكثرة السجود فإنه لا تسجد لله تعالى سجدة

ALUSI:96:19/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:19/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:19/r7.claim: On these and similar reports, several scholars hold that prostration is the best of the prayer's pillars.
ALUSI:96:19/r7.anchor: ولهذه الأخبار ونحوها ذهب غير واحد إلى أن السجود أفضل أركان الصلاة

ALUSI:96:19/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:19/r8.speaker: العز بن عبد السلام
ALUSI:96:19/r8.claim: Al-ʿIzz b. ʿAbd al-Salām, a leading Shāfiʿī imam, unusually held that supplication during prostration is obligatory.
ALUSI:96:19/r8.anchor: ومن الغريب أن العز بن عبد السلام من أجلة أئمة الشافعية قال بوجوب الدعاء فيه

ALUSI:96:19/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:19/r9.speaker: علي
ALUSI:96:19/r9.claim: Al-Baḥr reports that the Prophet prostrated when reciting 84:1 and this sūra; ʿAlī counted this sūra among the prostration verses, while Mālik prostrated over it privately.
ALUSI:96:19/r9.anchor: وفي هذه السورة وهي من العزائم عند علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه

BAGHAWI:96:19/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:19/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:19/r1.claim: The situation is not as Abu Jahl claims: do not obey him by abandoning prayer; prostrate in prayer to God and draw near to Him.
BAGHAWI:96:19/r1.anchor: ثم قال :{ كلا } ليس الأمر على ما عليه أبو جهل ، { لا تطعه } في ترك الصلاة ، { واسجد } صل لله

BAGHAWI:96:19/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:19/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI:96:19/r2.claim: The Prophet says a servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating and urges abundant supplication; Baghawi gives no grading.
BAGHAWI:96:19/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة " أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد ، فأكثروا الدعاء "

BAYDAWI:96:19/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:19/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:19/r1.claim: Kallā again rebukes the forbidding man; the Prophet should stay obedient, continue prostrating, and draw near to his Lord.
BAYDAWI:96:19/r1.anchor: { كلا } ردع أيضا للناهي { لا تطعه } أي اثبت أنت على طاعتك { واسجد } داوم على سجودك { واقترب } وتقرب إلى ربك

BAYDAWI:96:19/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:19/r2.speaker: الحديث
BAYDAWI:96:19/r2.claim: A hadith says a servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating; Bayḍāwī gives no grading or named transmitter.
BAYDAWI:96:19/r2.anchor: أقرب ما يكون العبد إلى ربه إذا سجد

BAYDAWI:96:19/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:19/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI:96:19/r3.claim: A report from the Prophet promises the reward of reciting the whole Mufaṣṣal to whoever recites Sūrat al-ʿAlaq; no grading is stated.
BAYDAWI:96:19/r3.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

BIQAI:96:19/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:19/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:19/r1.claim: The prior outcomes are all denied: the forbidding person will not stop the worshipper, threats will not reform him, and his gathering cannot save him; the rebuke tells him to desist.
BIQAI:96:19/r1.anchor: وكان الحكم في الأول أنه لا يجيبه إلى ترك الصلاة

BIQAI:96:19/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:19/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:19/r2.claim: The Prophet must not obey the person forbidding prayer or any other act of devotion; in a corrupt age he should attend to his own duty and turn away from others.
BIQAI:96:19/r2.anchor: أي في نهيه لك عن الطاعة بالصلاة أو غيرها

BIQAI:96:19/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:19/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:19/r3.claim: Because prostration is prayer's noblest part and can also mean worship generally, the command means to persist in prayer and personal submission; it signals victory for the Prophet and his followers over those who bar worship.

BIQAI:96:19/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:19/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:19/r4.claim: Prostration brings a servant closest to God; one should strive inwardly for nearness and love through every worship, especially prayer.
BIQAI:96:19/r4.anchor: أي اجتهد بسرك في بلوغ درجة القرب إلى ربك

BIQAI:96:19/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:19/r5.speaker: الإمام الغزالي
BIQAI:96:19/r5.claim: Al-Ghazālī reads the Prophet's refuge prayer as ascent from witnessing divine acts, to attributes, then to the divine essence; each stage leaves the self and all but God behind, until only God remains as praiser and praised.
BIQAI:96:19/r5.anchor: كما قال الإمام الغزالي في كتاب الشكر

BIQAI:96:19/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:19/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI:96:19/r6.claim: The Prophet's refuge prayer progresses through seeking refuge in God's pardon from punishment, pleasure from anger, and God from God, then recognizing that only God can praise God adequately.
BIQAI:96:19/r6.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  أعوذ بعفوك من عقوبتك

BIQAI:96:19/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:19/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:19/r7.claim: The Prophet viewed each station as deficient beside the next, sought forgiveness for it, and advanced beyond self-observation to God's exclusive praise; all things originate from Him and return to Him.
BIQAI:96:19/r7.anchor: لا يرقى من مرتبة إلى أخرى إلا ويرى الأولى بعداً

BIQAI:96:19/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:19/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI:96:19/r8.claim: The Prophet said that a veil comes over his heart and that he seeks God's forgiveness seventy times each day; Biqāʿī explains this as ascent through seventy stations, with earlier ones deficient beside later ones.
BIQAI:96:19/r8.anchor: وإليه الإشارة بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI:96:19/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:19/r9.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
BIQAI:96:19/r9.claim: ʿĀʾisha asked why the Prophet wept and exerted himself in prostration despite forgiveness of earlier and later sins; he answered that he should be a grateful servant, seeking further stations.
BIQAI:96:19/r9.anchor: ولما قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها : قد غفر الله لك ما تقدم من ذنبك

BIQAI:96:19/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:19/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:19/r10.claim: The Prophet's answer means that he seeks further spiritual increase, since gratitude brings increase, as God says in Abraham 14:7.

BIQAI:96:19/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:19/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:19/r11.claim: A servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating, so frequent supplication in prostration is likely to be answered.
BIQAI:96:19/r11.anchor: أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد

BIQAI:96:19/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:19/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:19/r12.claim: Since prayer requires recitation, devotion and recitation veil the worshipper from distractions, increase purity, and preserve his spiritual state from others.
BIQAI:96:19/r12.anchor: فإذا فعلت ذلك احتجبت عن الأغيار بحجاب منيع

BIQAI:96:19/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:19/r13.speaker: إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام
BIQAI:96:19/r13.claim: Biqāʿī cites Abraham's scriptures advising a wise person to guard his tongue, know his era, and attend to his own affairs.
BIQAI:96:19/r13.anchor: ما في صحف إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام

BIQAI:96:19/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:19/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:19/r14.claim: The sūra's ending returns fittingly to its beginning.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.claim: Majūs and Yahūd are nouns used only for a tribe, with feminine gender prevailing; Imruʾ al-Qays’s simile ‘like the fire of Majūs’ illustrates the usage.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.claim: When Majūs names a man, it is diptote, just like ʿAmmān.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.anchor: بمجوس لم تصرفه كما لا تصرفه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.claim: The definite forms al-Yahūd and al-Majūs use the article as in nisba adjectives, with the nisba yāʾs deleted; without the article, majūs is indefinite, like majūsiyyīn without its article.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.claim: Naṣārā is an indefinite plural of naṣrān and naṣrāna; prose normally uses the nisba forms, but the plural omits the nisba yāʾs, like nadāmā from nadmān, and means al-naṣrāniyyīn.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.anchor: وأما نصارى فنكرة وإنما نصارى جمع نصران ونصرانة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالميقعإلااسماللقبيلة)#5.claim: Poetry uses naṣārā as an indefinite; a cited line describes the cupbearer of naṣārā, and another poetic example attests the feminine singular naṣrāna.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.claim: Al-Khalīl explains tribal plurals in wāw-nūn, such as al-Ashʿarūn and al-Aʿjamūn, as analogical additions alongside broken plurals; the pattern is not productive for every such name.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.anchor: سألت الخليل عن قولهم الأشعرون فقال إنما ألحقوا الواو والنون كما كسروا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.claim: One possible account of maqtawīn is retention of the original form, parallel to maqātawa; Abū al-Khaṭṭāb reports this word from Arabs, though not all Arabs know it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.anchor: فإن شئت قلت جاءوا به على الأصل كما قالوا مقاتوة حدثنا بذلك أبو الخطاب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.claim: Alternatively, maqtawīn may follow madharwīn because it has no singular used independently.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.claim: Al-Khalīl analyzes naṣārā as a plural of naṣrī and naṣrān, like nadmān/nadāmā and mihri/mahārā, with a yāʾ dropped and replaced by alif.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.anchor: وأما النصارى فإنه جماع نصري ونصران

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.claim: Sībawayh prefers deriving naṣārā from the attested feminine singular naṣrāna, like ashʿath/ashāʿith; he calls this more analogical because naṣrī is unattested.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.anchor: هذا قول الخليل وأما الذي نوجهه عليه فأنه جاء على نصرانة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجمعبالواووالنونوتكسي.claim: Abū al-Akhzar al-Ḥammānī’s verse, which explicitly uses naṣrāna, supports Sībawayh’s analysis of naṣārā as a plural of naṣrāna.

DURR:96:19/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:19/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR:96:19/r1.claim: Zayd b. Aslam reads “prostrate” as addressed to Muhammad, but “draw near” as addressed to Abū Jahl as a threat.
DURR:96:19/r1.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم قال :{ واسجد } أنت يا محمد { واقترب } أنت يا أبا جهل يتوعده

DURR:96:19/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:19/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:96:19/r2.claim: Mujāhid says a servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating, citing the command to prostrate and draw near.
DURR:96:19/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد

DURR:96:19/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:19/r3.speaker: عثمان بن أبي العاصي
DURR:96:19/r3.claim: ʿUthmān b. Abī al-ʿĀṣī says the Prophet’s last instruction on appointing him over al-Ṭāʾif was to shorten people’s prayers, reciting al-ʿAlaq or similar sūras.
DURR:96:19/r3.anchor: عن عثمان بن أبي العاصي قال : آخر كلام كلمني به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ استعملني على الطائف

IBNASHUR:96:6/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r9.speaker: الحربي
IBNASHUR:96:6/r9.claim: Al-Ḥarbī, as quoted by al-Suhaylī, says that before the Night Journey the Prophet prayed once before sunset and once before sunrise.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r9.anchor: ذكر الحربي أن الصلاة قبل الإسراء كانت صلاة قبل غروب الشمس ( أي العصر ) وصلاة قبل طلوعها ( أي الصبح )

IBNASHUR:96:6/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r10.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
IBNASHUR:96:6/r10.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Sallām agrees that the Prophet prayed before sunset and before sunrise; al-Suhaylī also says the Night Journey and obligation of five prayers came a year before the Hijra.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r10.anchor: وقال يحيى بن سلام مثله ،  وقال :  كان الإسراء وفرض الصلوات الخمس قبل الهجرة بعام

IBNASHUR:96:6/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:6/r11.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr identifies the prayer as an unregulated pre-obligation form, distinct from the five daily prayers, that included prostration and was performed publicly where polytheists could see it, provoking Abū Jahl.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r11.anchor: فالوجه أن تكون الصلاة التي كان يصليها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاة غير الصلوات الخمس بل كانت هيئة غير مضبوطة بكيفية وفيها سجود

IBNASHUR:96:19/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:19/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:19/r1.claim: Kallā cancels the suggestion that Abū Jahl can summon his assembly, reinforcing the preceding challenge that he will not carry it out.
IBNASHUR:96:19/r1.anchor: و { كَلاّ } ردع لإِبطال ما تضمنه قوله :  { فليدع ناديه } ،  أي وليس بفاعل

IBNASHUR:96:19/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:19/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:19/r3.claim: The Prophet is told not to abandon prayer at the Sacred Mosque or fear Abū Jahl: obedience stands for the caution that fear would produce, and Abū Jahl cannot harm him.
IBNASHUR:96:19/r3.anchor: أي لا تترك صلاتك في المسجد الحرام ولا تخش منه .

IBNASHUR:96:19/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:19/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:19/r4.claim: The command to prostrate reinforces the command not to obey the threat and emphasizes the importance of prayer.
IBNASHUR:96:19/r4.anchor: وأكد قوله :  { لا تطعه } بجملة { واسجد } اهتماماً بالصلاة

IBNASHUR:96:19/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:19/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:19/r5.claim: Prayer pleases God and brings the worshipper near to Him; the iftiʿāl form conveys exertion and seeking, so the command means to strive for closeness through prayer.
IBNASHUR:96:19/r5.anchor: وعطف عليه { واقترب } للتنويه بما في الصلاة من مرضاة الله تعالى بحيث جعل المصلي مقترباً من الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA:96:19/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r1.claim: Kalla rejects the unbeliever's speech and conduct; Muhammad is told not to heed his prohibition or words.
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r1.anchor: ثم قال تعالى لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم : [ كلا ] ردا على قول هذا الكافر وأفعاله [ لا تطعه ]

IBNATIYYA:96:19/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r2.claim: Prostrate to God and draw near through prostration, obedience, and righteous deeds.
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r2.anchor: لا تلتفت إلى نهيه وكلامه ، ( واسجد ) لربك ، ( واقترب ) إليه بسجودك وبالطاعة وبالأعمال الصالحة

IBNATIYYA:96:19/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r3.claim: The Prophet says the servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating and urges abundant supplication then, which is likely to be answered.
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه إذا سجد

IBNATIYYA:96:19/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r4.claim: Mujahid cites the command prostrate and draw near in support of the instruction to approach God.
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r4.anchor: وقالَه مجاهد ، قال : ألم تسمعوا ( واسجد واقترب )

IBNATIYYA:96:19/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r5.speaker: جماعة من أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r5.claim: A group of scholars, transmitted by Ibn Wahb, take prostrate as addressed to Muhammad and draw near as addressed to Abu Jahl, challenging him to see how he will be destroyed.
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r5.anchor: وروى ابن وهب عن جماعة من أهل العلم أن قوله تعالى : [ واسجد ] خطاب لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA:96:19/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r6.speaker: جماعة من أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r6.claim: A group of scholars, including Ibn Wahb among Malik's companions, recognize a prostration of recitation at the end of this sura.
IBNATIYYA:96:19/r6.anchor: وهذه السورة فيها سجدة عند جماعة من أهل العلم منهم ابن وهب من أصحاب مالك

IBNKATHIR:96:19/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:19/r1.speaker: author
