IBNKATHIR:96:19/r1.claim: Muhammad must not obey the command to stop abundant, continual worship; he may pray wherever he wishes without concern because God protects and supports him.
IBNKATHIR:96:19/r1.anchor: لا تطعه فيما ينهاك عنه من المداومة على العبادة وكثرتها ، وصل حيث شئت ولا تباله

IBNKATHIR:96:19/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:19/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR:96:19/r2.claim: The Prophet says a servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating, so worshippers should make abundant supplication.
IBNKATHIR:96:19/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR:96:19/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:19/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:19/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir recalls that the Prophet prostrated when reciting al-Inshiqaq and Iqra.
IBNKATHIR:96:19/r3.anchor: وتقدم أيضا : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يسجد

MAWARDI:96:19/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
MAWARDI:96:19/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra glosses “do not obey him” as not obeying Abu Jahl.
MAWARDI:96:19/r1.anchor: قال أبو هريرة : كلا لا تطع أبا جهل في أمره .

MAWARDI:96:19/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r2.claim: One possible sense is not to accept Abu Jahl's words if he accommodates you, or his opinion if he draws near.
MAWARDI:96:19/r2.anchor: أحدهما : لا تقبل قوله إن داراك ، ولا رأيه إن قاربك .

MAWARDI:96:19/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r3.claim: Another possible sense is not to answer his speech or retaliate for his actions.
MAWARDI:96:19/r3.anchor: الثاني : لا تجبه عن قوله ، ولا تقابله على فعله ،

MAWARDI:96:19/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r4.speaker: النبي
MAWARDI:96:19/r4.claim: The cited Prophet's supplication uses atiʿ in the sense of answering a prayer: he asks God not to answer a traveler praying for rain to stop, since people would perish.
MAWARDI:96:19/r4.anchor: ومنه ما روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : " اللهم لا تطع فينا مسافراً "

MAWARDI:96:19/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI:96:19/r5.claim: Zayd b. Aslam reads the commands as Muhammad prostrating in prayer and Abu Jahl drawing near to the Fire.
MAWARDI:96:19/r5.anchor: أحدهما : اسجد أنت يا محمد مصلياً ، واقترب أنت يا أبا جهل من النار ، قاله زيد بن أسلم .

MAWARDI:96:19/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r6.claim: The Prophet is commanded to prostrate in prayer and draw near to his Lord; the servant is nearest to God while prostrating.
MAWARDI:96:19/r6.anchor: الثاني : اسجد أنت يا محمد في صلاتك لتقرب من ربك ، فإن أقرب ما يكون العبد إلى الله تعالى إذا سجد له .

MAWARDI:96:19/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r7.claim: This verse contains a prostration of recitation.

MAWARDI:96:19/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:96:19/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that 84 verses were revealed about Abu Jahl, 104 about al-Walid b. al-Mughira, and 32 about al-Nadr b. al-Harith.
MAWARDI:96:19/r8.anchor: روى جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال : أنزل في أبي جهل أربع وثمانون آية

MAWARDI:96:19/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r9.claim: Most scholars hold that this was the first sura revealed to the Messenger.
MAWARDI:96:19/r9.anchor: إذا كانت هذه أول سورة نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قول الأكثرين

MAWARDI:96:19/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r10.claim: A chronological report attributed to ʿAta al-Khurasani calls the Qurʾanic revelation order from Mecca and Medina its sequence, and gives 85 Meccan suras, beginning with al-ʿAlaq.
MAWARDI:96:19/r10.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني قال : بلغنا أن هذا ما نزل من القرآن بمكة والمدينة الأول فالأول

MAWARDI:96:19/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r11.claim: The Meccan sequence continues al-Qalam, al-Muzzammil, al-Muddaththir, al-Masad, al-Takwir, al-Aʿla, al-Layl, al-Fajr, al-Duha, al-Sharh, al-ʿAsr, and al-ʿAdiyat.
MAWARDI:96:19/r11.anchor: ثم " ن والقلم " ، " المزمل " ، " المدثر " ، " تبت " ،

MAWARDI:96:19/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r12.claim: It next lists al-Inshirah, al-ʿAsr, al-ʿAdiyat, al-Kawthar, al-Takathur, al-Maʿun, al-Kafirun, al-Fil, al-Falaq, al-Ikhlas, al-Najm, and ʿAbasa.
MAWARDI:96:19/r12.anchor: " ألم نشرح " ، " العصر " ، " العاديات " ، " الكوثر " ، " ألهاكم " ، " أرأيت " ، " الكافرون " ، " الفيل "

MAWARDI:96:19/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r13.claim: The sequence then names al-Qadr, al-Shams, al-Tin, Quraysh, al-Qariʿa, al-Qiyama, al-Humaza, al-Mursalat, Qaf, al-Balad, al-Tariq, and al-Qamar.

MAWARDI:96:19/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r14.claim: It continues with Sad, al-Aʿraf, al-Jinn, Ya-Sin, al-Furqan, Fatir, Maryam, Ta-Ha, al-Waqiʿa, al-Shuʿaraʾ, al-Naml, and al-Qasas.
MAWARDI:96:19/r14.anchor: " ص " ، " الأعراف " ، " قل أوحي " ، " يس " ، " الفرقان "

MAWARDI:96:19/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r15.claim: The order proceeds through Banu Israʾil, Yunus, Hud, Yusuf, al-Hijr, al-Anʿam, al-Saffat, Luqman, Sabaʾ, al-Zumar, and al-Muʾmin.
MAWARDI:96:19/r15.anchor: " يوسف " ، " الحجر " ، " الأنعام " ، " الصافات " ، " لقمان " ، " سبأ " ، " الزمر " ،

MAWARDI:96:19/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r16.claim: Next come Ha-Mim al-Sajda, ʿAyn-Sin-Qaf, al-Zukhruf, al-Dukhan, al-Jathiya, al-Ahqaf, al-Dhariyat, al-Ghashiya, al-Kahf, al-Nahl, and Nuh.
MAWARDI:96:19/r16.anchor: " الزخرف " ، " الدخان " ، " الجاثية " ، " الأحقاف " ، " الذاريات " ، " الغاشية "

MAWARDI:96:19/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r17.claim: The Meccan list concludes with Ibrahim, al-Anbiyaʾ, al-Muʾminun, al-Sajda, al-Tur, al-Mulk, al-Haqqa, Saʾala Saʾil, al-Nabaʾ, al-Naziʿat, al-Infitar, al-Inshiqaq, al-Rum, al-ʿAnkabut, and al-Mutaffifin.
MAWARDI:96:19/r17.anchor: " نوح " ، " إبراهيم " ، " الأنبياء " ، " قد أفلح " {[7]} ، " السجدة " ، " الطور "

MAWARDI:96:19/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r18.claim: The report gives 27 Medinan suras, beginning with al-Baqara, al-Anfal, Aal ʿImran, al-Ahzab, al-Mumtahana, al-Nisaʾ, al-Zalzala, al-Hadid, and Muhammad.
MAWARDI:96:19/r18.anchor: وكان فيما نزل بالمدينة البقرة ، ثم " الأنفال " ، " آل عمران " ، " الأحزاب " ، " الممتحنة " ، " النساء "

MAWARDI:96:19/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r19.claim: Its Medinan sequence continues al-Raʿd, al-Rahman, al-Insan, al-Talaq, al-Bayyina, al-Hashr, al-Nasr, al-Nur, and al-Hajj.

MAWARDI:96:19/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r20.claim: The final Medinan entries are al-Munafiqun, al-Mujadila, al-Hujurat, al-Tahrim, al-Jumuʿa, al-Saff, al-Fath, al-Maʾida, and Baraʾa.

MAWARDI:96:19/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:19/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:19/r21.claim: The report omits al-Fatiha; revelation-order accounts differ widely, but the author includes this one because he found it the fullest and most satisfying.
MAWARDI:96:19/r21.anchor: ولم تكن الفاتحة والله أعلم ضمن ما ذكره ، وقد اختلف الناس في نزول السور اختلافاً كثيراً ، لكن وجدت هذا الحديث أوفى وأشفى فذكرته .

NASAFI:96:19/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:19/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:19/r1.claim: Do not obey Abū Jahl: remain steadfast in disobeying him, as in the command not to obey the deniers.
NASAFI:96:19/r1.anchor: { لاَ تُطِعْهُ } أي اثبت على ما أنت عليه من عصيانه

NASAFI:96:19/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:19/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:19/r2.claim: “Prostrate” means persist in prostration, that is, continue praying.

NASAFI:96:19/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:19/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:19/r3.claim: Draw near to your Lord by prostration.

NASAFI:96:19/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:19/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:19/r4.claim: A hadith says that the servant is nearest to his Lord when prostrating.
NASAFI:96:19/r4.anchor: فإن أقرب ما يكون العبد إلى ربه إذا سجد

QURTUBI:96:19/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:19/r1.claim: Kallā rejects Abu Jahl’s assumption that he can prevent the Prophet through his power.
QURTUBI:96:19/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : " كلا " أي ليس الأمر على ما يظنه أبو جهل

QURTUBI:96:19/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:19/r2.claim: The Prophet must not obey Abu Jahl’s demand that he stop praying.
QURTUBI:96:19/r2.anchor: " لا تطعه " أي فيما دعاك إليه من ترك الصلاة

QURTUBI:96:19/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:19/r3.claim: The command to prostrate means to pray to God.

QURTUBI:96:19/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:19/r4.claim: Approach God through obedience and worship.
QURTUBI:96:19/r4.anchor: " واقترب " أي تقرب إلى اللّه جل ثناؤه بالطاعة والعبادة

QURTUBI:96:19/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:19/r5.claim: Another view says to draw near to God through supplication while prostrating.
QURTUBI:96:19/r5.anchor: وقيل : المعنى : إذا سجدت فاقترب من الله بالدعاء

QURTUBI:96:19/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI:96:19/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports from Abū Hurayra that the servant is nearest and most beloved to his Lord when prostrating with his forehead on the ground.
QURTUBI:96:19/r6.anchor: أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه ،   وأحبه إليه ،   جبهته في الأرض

QURTUBI:96:19/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r7.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI:96:19/r7.claim: Prostration is the utmost servitude and humility; since God has absolute majesty, the worshipper’s abasement brings nearness to Paradise and His abode.
QURTUBI:96:19/r7.anchor: قال علماؤنا : وإنما كان ذلك لأنها نهاية العبودية والذلة ،   ولله غاية العزة

QURTUBI:96:19/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r8.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI:96:19/r8.claim: A ṣaḥīḥ hadith says to glorify God in bowing and strive in supplication during prostration, where prayers are likely to be answered.
QURTUBI:96:19/r8.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح : أن النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم قال : [ أما الركوع فعظموا فيه الرب

QURTUBI:96:19/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r9.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI:96:19/r9.claim: A poem expresses the paradox that humble submission before God is itself a source of honor.
QURTUBI:96:19/r9.anchor: وإذا تذللت الرقاب تواضعًا *** منا إليك فعِزُّهَا في ذُلِّهَا

QURTUBI:96:19/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r10.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
QURTUBI:96:19/r10.claim: Zayd b. Aslam reads the command as telling Muhammad to pray while Abu Jahl approaches the Fire.
QURTUBI:96:19/r10.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم : اسجد أنت يا محمد مصليا ،   واقترب أنت يا أبا جهل من النار

QURTUBI:96:19/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r11.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI:96:19/r11.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says the apparent sense is the prostration of prayer, given the passage’s context about prayer.
QURTUBI:96:19/r11.anchor: قال ابن العربي : " والظاهر أنه سجود الصلاة " لقوله تعالى

QURTUBI:96:19/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:19/r12.claim: The ṣaḥīḥ report from Abū Hurayra explicitly says he prostrated with the Prophet in al-Inshiqāq and Iqraʾ, establishing this as a recitation prostration.
QURTUBI:96:19/r12.anchor: من رواية مسلم وغيره من الأئمة عن أبي هريرة أنه قال : سجدت مع رسول الله

QURTUBI:96:19/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r13.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI:96:19/r13.claim: A report from ʿAlī lists four decisive prostrations: alif-lām-mīm, Ḥā-mīm Tanzīl, al-Najm, and Iqraʾ.
QURTUBI:96:19/r13.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه ،   قال : عزائم السجود أربع : " ألم " و " حم تنزيل

QURTUBI:96:19/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r14.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI:96:19/r14.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says that if ʿAlī’s report is authentic, it would also require the second prostration in al-Ḥajj despite its association with bowing.
QURTUBI:96:19/r14.anchor: وقال ابن العربي : وهذا إن صح يلزم عليه السجود الثاني من سورة " الحج "

QURTUBI:96:19/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r15.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI:96:19/r15.claim: Ibn Nāfiʿ and Muṭarrif report that Mālik would privately prostrate at the end of this sūra.
QURTUBI:96:19/r15.anchor: وقد قال ابن نافع ومطرف : وكان مالك يسجد في خاصة نفسه بخاتمة هذه السورة

QURTUBI:96:19/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r16.speaker: ابن وهب
QURTUBI:96:19/r16.claim: Ibn Wahb considered the final prostration of the sūra one of the decisive prostrations.

QURTUBI:96:19/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:19/r17.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI:96:19/r17.claim: A report through Mālik, Rabīʿa, and Nāfiʿ says that when Iqraʾ was revealed, Muʿādh was told to write it; the tablet, pen, and inkwell prostrated and prayed for the revelation’s blessing, then Muʿādh and the Prophet prostrated.
QURTUBI:96:19/r17.anchor: وقد روينا من حديث مالك بن أنس عن ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال : لما أنزل الله تعالى

RAZI:96:19/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:19/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:96:19/r1.claim: Kallā may rebuke Abu Jahl and deny that his assembly can help if summoned; he is too lowly to resist the Prophet.
RAZI:96:19/r1.anchor: وقيل : معناه لن يصل إلى ما يتصلف به من أنه يدعو ناديه ولئن دعاهم لن ينفعوه ولن ينصروه ، وهو أذل وأحقر من أن يقاومك

RAZI:96:19/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:19/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:96:19/r2.claim: Alternatively, Abu Jahl will not achieve his wish that Muhammad obey him by stopping prayer.
RAZI:96:19/r2.anchor: ويحتمل : لن ينال ما يتمنى من طاعتك له حين نهاك عن الصلاة

RAZI:96:19/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:19/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:96:19/r3.claim: Kallā may also be understood as alā, an alerting “indeed” or “lo.”

RAZI:96:19/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:19/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:96:19/r4.claim: The command not to obey Abu Jahl echoes the command not to obey those who deny the truth.
RAZI:96:19/r4.anchor: ثم قال : { لا تطعه } وهو كقوله : { فلا تطع المكذبين }

RAZI:96:19/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:19/r5.speaker: أكثر أهل التأويل
RAZI:96:19/r5.claim: Most exegetes understand “prostrate” as praying and devoting one's action and proclamation to God's worship, while relying on God's support against the enemy.
RAZI:96:19/r5.anchor: وعند أكثر أهل التأويل أراد به صل وتوفر على عبادة الله تعالى فعلا وإبلاغا

RAZI:96:19/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:19/r6.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI:96:19/r6.claim: Some say the command means humility and submission.

RAZI:96:19/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:19/r7.speaker: آخرون
RAZI:96:19/r7.claim: Others take it as the literal prostration within prayer.
RAZI:96:19/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل المراد نفس السجود في الصلاة

RAZI:96:19/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:19/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:96:19/r8.claim: The main interpretation is to seek nearness in rank with one's Lord through prostration.
RAZI:96:19/r8.anchor: والمراد وابتغ بسجودك قرب المنزلة من ربك

RAZI:96:19/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:19/r9.speaker: النبي
RAZI:96:19/r9.claim: A Prophetic report says the servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating.
RAZI:96:19/r9.anchor: وفي الحديث : «أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه إذا سجد »

RAZI:96:19/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:19/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:96:19/r10.claim: Another taunting reading orders Muhammad to prostrate and Abu Jahl to approach, so he can witness the angels seize him and become more enraged at the prayer he tried to prevent.
RAZI:96:19/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم المراد : اسجد يا محمد ، واقترب يا أبا جهل منه حتى تبصر ما ينالك من أخذ الزبانية إياك

RAZI:96:19/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:19/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:96:19/r11.claim: On this taunting reading, Abu Jahl is told to put his foot on the praying Prophet, like the phrase about believers enraging unbelievers.
RAZI:96:19/r11.anchor: ثم قال عند ذلك : { واقترب } منه يا أبا جهل وضع قدمك عليه
